answer.question: What should I check before artificial turf goes into a Louviers yard?
answer.answer: Start with the water district. It adopted four drought stages on 21 April 2026 and sends written notice when one takes effect. At Stage 2 no new lawns or shrubs may be planted, but turf isn't part of that rule.

blocks.h2: Four stages, each with its own watering days.
blocks.takeaway: The water district adopted four drought stages on 21 April 2026 and sends written notice when one starts. Find your notice, or ask the district, before planning anything that needs water.
paras: Louviers is unincorporated Douglas County (Wikipedia), and its water comes from its own special district. On 21 April 2026 the district's board adopted drought and water shortage restrictions in four steps: voluntary, Stage 1, Stage 2 and Stage 3. When the board puts a stage in force, every customer gets written notice of the stage, its start date and its rules.

Stage 1 limits homes to Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, and nobody waters from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Trees, shrubs, perennials and vegetable gardens can still be watered any day by hand-held hose or drip. The voluntary step is the same list, unenforced.

Stage 2 cuts homes to Tuesday and Saturday and stops new planting: no new lawns, trees, perennials, shrubs, annual beds or vegetable gardens. Stage 3 starts rationing, and all outdoor water use may be prohibited. The district's rules page doesn't say which stage, if any, is in force as of 12 September 2026. Find your notice, or call the district at 303-482-1002 ext. 5, before you plan anything that needs water.

blocks.h2: Turf doesn't wait on a stage. New beds might.
blocks.takeaway: No stage limits laying turf, edging or paths, but at Stage 2 a new planted border has to wait. For a dog area, ask the district how it treats rinsing the turf.
paras: The restrictions cover water supplied by the district and don't mention artificial turf, which is neither planted nor watered — laying turf, edging and paths isn't limited by any stage. What a stage controls is what goes in around it. If Stage 2 is in force when you're ready to start, the planted border you drew beside the turf has to wait, and existing shrubs move to the Tuesday and Saturday schedule, by hand or drip. If no stage is in force, nothing in the resolution stops new beds — ask the district which stage applies before you commit to a planting plan.

The board can also grant written variances for specific uses or seasonal needs. Its next meeting is a special session on 15 September 2026, followed by regular meetings set for 27 October and 17 November (Louviers Water and Sanitation District).

For a dog area, plan the rinse separately from the planting question. Stage 1 allows power washing only on assigned watering days, and Stage 2 bans using water to clean outdoor impervious surfaces such as sidewalks and patios. Neither stage names synthetic turf or a rinse, so ask the district how it treats cleaning a pet area. Our guide to rinsing pet turf under watering restrictions covers what to ask.

blocks.h2: Water lines were replaced this year. Find yours before anyone digs.
blocks.takeaway: The district has been replacing water lines, and a refilled trench is ground the base must account for. Ask whether yours is done, call 811 before digging, and show us any fresh trench.
paras: The district has been replacing water mains and service lines in parts of Louviers. Its notice of 11 February 2026 set work from about 10 March through about August 2026, with some homes getting a new service line and meter together. The full job covers about 12,000 feet of aging galvanized steel pipe, 86 service lines and 15 fire hydrants (federal funding award).

A trench dug and refilled this year is ground a turf base has to account for. Ask the district whether your line and meter are done or still on the list — call 303-482-1002 ext. 5, or check the board's 15 September agenda, which carries an engineer's construction report, so the dates may have moved. Call 811 before excavation, and point out any fresh trench on the free visit so we can prepare the site and build the base with it in mind.

blocks.h2: Mostly well-drained ground, with a heavier patch on the slopes.
blocks.takeaway: Most of Louviers drains well, but one steeper pocket has swelling clay, so nearby yards can need different preparation. We check yours at the free visit and set the fall away from the house.
paras: Louviers sits at 5,614 feet, with US 85 on its eastern edge (Wikipedia). USDA soil maps put the center of town on loamy alluvial land: well drained, carrying a moderate share of clay, and not prone to much swelling when it gets wet (USDA Soil Data Access).

Within about half a mile, most of the surrounding ground drains even faster — sandy Blakeland-Orsa soil and gravelly Newlin soil on the slopes both take water in quickly. One small pocket, on steeper ground nearby, carries a heavier, slow-draining soil that happens to share the town's name: Louviers soil, high in clay and prone to swelling when it's wet.

So yards a few streets apart can need different preparation. The free visit checks what's under yours, and we build the base for that soil with the fall running away from the house. See what goes under artificial turf for the layers.

servicesNote: Compare a lawn, a dog area or a backyard putting green — none of it waits on the district's watering days to go in.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Louviers, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Louviers, CO. Turf itself doesn't need any of the district's watering days to go in, but check with Louviers Water and Sanitation District on which drought stage is in force before you plan the rest of the yard. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: What happens if I water on the wrong day in Louviers?
faq.a: A first violation brings a written notice. The second and third add a violation charge on your water bill, and the third notice offers a hearing. At the fourth, the district may shut off your water until the violation is corrected and charges are paid, and you pay the shutoff and turn-on fees (2026 restrictions). The district's rates page doesn't list the charge's amount, so ask.

faq.q: Is there a rebate for artificial turf in Louviers?
faq.a: We found no rebate program listed on the district's website, so ask the district before you count on one. Across the metro, most providers' lawn programs exclude artificial turf, and our Denver-area rebate guide shows who pays and who doesn't.

faq.q: Who handles permits for turf in Louviers?
faq.a: Louviers has no town government of its own; Douglas County governs it. Ask the county whether your layout, a retaining wall or a change in grade needs a permit, and ask the water district about anything that touches your service line or meter.
